title: HarnessIssue — one immutable post-run observation (sole owner: observer)
description: Growth happens after the run (V3-D10). A real harness defect or burden may be recorded here; it never changes the active WorkSpec, plan, profile, checks or verdict, and it is not part of any live run's evidence. Only a post-run user ISSUE_TRIAGE decision routes it (contract §11) — which is why this document carries NO routing, state, resolution or triage field of its own. Their absence is enforced by additionalProperties:false rather than left to convention: a status field here would quietly become a lifecycle, and V3 has no Retrospective state machine, dedup registry or automatic maintenance stage (N2-A10, N2-A11). An issue is a thing observed, recorded once and thereafter read-only; what to DO about it is a user decision living in its own typed document.

run_id.description: The run during which the defect or burden was observed. This binds the observation to a context; it does not make the issue part of that run's evidence.

kind.description: A defect is the harness doing something wrong; a burden is the harness costing more than it protects. The second exists because plan §10 makes it an adoption criterion — if measured control effort dominates the protected document work the decision is REVISE_V3, and that judgment needs recorded instances rather than an impression.

statement.description: What was observed, in the observer's own words.

evidence_refs.description: At least one exact document supporting the observation. Required and non-empty: an evidence-free issue is an opinion, and routing opinions into workflow, profile or core changes is how a harness grows features nobody could later justify (V3-D10).

observed_after.description: The terminal status the run had reached when this was recorded. Narrowed from the shared status enum to the two terminal values, which makes 'post-run only' a property of the document rather than a rule someone has to remember: an issue claiming to be observed mid-run is unrepresentable, so it cannot be used to influence a run in flight (N2-A10).
